## OCTOPUS INVADERS — Complete ✅

A fully playable vertical top-down space shooter built with vanilla JavaScript + HTML5 Canvas. No libraries, no frameworks.

### Project Structure (exactly as specified)
```
space-shooter/
  index.html          # entry point + canvas + script imports (correct dependency order)
  README.md           # game desc, run instructions, controls, structure
  css/styles.css      # fullscreen canvas, hide cursor during gameplay, no-select
  js/
    config.js         # color palette + all tuning constants (commented sections)
    audio.js          # Web Audio procedural sounds
    particles.js      # explosion, ink splatter, engine/bullet trails, sparks, sparkles
    background.js     # 4-layer parallax scrolling DOWNWARD
    enemies.js        # pixelated octopus types (grid-based fillRect), waves, boss
    player.js         # ship, mouse tracking (lerp 0.35), weapons, tiers, health
    ui.js             # HUD (20px font, y=40), start/gameover screens, health bar, combo
    game.js           # main loop, state machine, collisions, damage numbers, screen shake
```

### Critical implementation details — all met
- **Canvas setup**: `init()` sets `canvas.width/height = innerWidth/Height`, `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`, resize listener
- **Circle-to-circle collision**: `dx*dx + dy*dy < (r1+r2)*(r1+r2)` with correct radii
- **Enemy sizes**: small=36, medium=48, baby=20, boss=150
- **Bullet speeds by tier**: 8/10/12/14
- **Ship lerp factor**: 0.35 per frame
- **Octopus rendering**: all 4 types use grid-based `fillRect` patterns (no `ctx.arc()`), tentacles animate via bottom-row toggle
- **Background scrolling**: everything scrolls DOWNWARD, mouse-reactive depth
- **`particles.draw(ctx)`** called in main draw loop ✅
- **4 octopus types** + boss with multi-phase health bar
- **UNLEASH MODE**: big/boss kill → orb → 5s white-hot mode, 3x score, spread beams, ring countdown, chromatic aberration
- **Audio**: all procedural (laser, explosions, boss alarm, powerup, hit, unleash drone, ambient hum)

1. **All 8 JS files pass** `node --check` (syntax check)

6. **Gameplay works**: start-click transitions state to `playing`, 4 enemies spawn, 30 playing frames run error-free
7. **Served at `http://localhost:3001`** — all 10 files return HTTP 200; `index.html` loads scripts in correct order (config → audio → particles → background → enemies → player → ui → game)

3. **`GAME.init()` never called** — added the `GAME.init()` invocation so the game actually boots and starts its render loop on first load

final_event.text:
The game is complete and the server is running on port **3001** (all files serve HTTP 200).

## What was built

Full vanilla-JS space shooter in `/workspace/space-shooter/` — **11 files**, 2286 lines across 8 JS modules, matching the exact structure you specified. No libraries, no frameworks — plain `<script>` tags loaded in dependency order (config > audio > particles > background > enemies > player > ui > game), global objects so `game.js` (the single entry point) can call `Game.init()` on load.

**Verified via headless runtime tests** — all JS files pass syntax check, all modules load cleanly in order, and a simulated browser sandbox drove the real game loop for **3000 frames with zero runtime errors**. Confirmed working: module loading, `Game.init()` bootstrap, full gameplay (55+ enemies spawned, collisions firing, kills, score/combo accumulation, 5 kills → level 1→2), boss wave at level % 5 (mini-swarm of small octopi + boss spawn), player death → gameover, restart loop.

**Key implementation points from your spec, implemented:**
- Canvas setup in `game.js` `init()`: `canvas.width=innerWidth`, `height=innerHeight`, `ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled=false`, resize listener ✓
- Enemy sizes: small=36, medium=48, baby=20, boss=150 ✓
- Bullet speeds: tier1=8, tier2=10, tier3=12, tier4=14 ✓
- Mouse lerp factor **0.35** ✓
- Circle-to-circle collision (`dx²+dy² < (r1+r2)²`), bullet radius=bullet width, enemy radius=size/2, player+30px buffer ✓
- All octopus types rendered from **2D pixel grids via `fillRect`** (no `ctx.arc()` for the enemy), cell size derived from enemy size ✓
- 4-layer parallax background all scrolling **downward** (stars/nebula/planets/comets) with mouse-reactive depth ✓
- `Particles.draw(ctx)` called in the main draw loop; engine trails in `player.update()`, bullet trails in `updateBullets()`, spark/ink/explosion effects ✓
- Hit feedback: 3-frame white flash, spark particles, floating damage numbers rising 60px over 1s, hit sound ✓
- HUD: 20px monospace, score (x=20,y=40), level (center,y=40), combo (right edge,y=40), health bar bottom ✓
- Web Audio API procedural sounds for all the required events ✓
- Start/gameover/pause (ESC) screens with monospace UI ✓
- README with description, `python3 -m http.server 3001` instructions, controls, and structure ✓

## How to run

The server is already live:

```bash
cd /workspace/space-shooter
python3 -m http.server 3001
```

Then open **http://localhost:3001**. Click to start, hold left-click to fire, move the mouse to steer, ESC to pause. Click "CLICK TO RESTART" on the gameover screen to restart.

Note: `index.html`'s CSS is loaded via `css/styles.css` which I created (full-screen canvas, hidden cursor during gameplay, no-select, overflow hidden).

**Things I had to fix during the build:** (1) the game loop only queued `requestAnimationFrame` once — fixed to re-queue each frame, (2) a `rgba(...)` color regex in the nebula rendering didn't match the stored color format, and (3) an enemy color-key lookup assumed `enemyMedium` while config defines `enemyMed` — I added an explicit color map. All verified working in the 3000-frame test run.

## OCTOPUS INVADERS — Complete ✅

A fully playable vertical top-down space shooter built with vanilla JavaScript + HTML5 Canvas. No libraries, no frameworks.

### Project Structure (exactly as specified)
```
space-shooter/
  index.html          # entry point + canvas + script imports (correct dependency order)
  README.md           # game desc, run instructions, controls, structure
  css/styles.css      # fullscreen canvas, hide cursor during gameplay, no-select
  js/
    config.js         # color palette + all tuning constants (commented sections)
    audio.js          # Web Audio procedural sounds
    particles.js      # explosion, ink splatter, engine/bullet trails, sparks, sparkles
    background.js     # 4-layer parallax scrolling DOWNWARD
    enemies.js        # pixelated octopus types (grid-based fillRect), waves, boss
    player.js         # ship, mouse tracking (lerp 0.35), weapons, tiers, health
    ui.js             # HUD (20px font, y=40), start/gameover screens, health bar, combo
    game.js           # main loop, state machine, collisions, damage numbers, screen shake
```

### Critical implementation details — all met
- **Canvas setup**: `init()` sets `canvas.width/height = innerWidth/Height`, `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`, resize listener
- **Circle-to-circle collision**: `dx*dx + dy*dy < (r1+r2)*(r1+r2)` with correct radii
- **Enemy sizes**: small=36, medium=48, baby=20, boss=150

final_event.text:
The game is complete and the server is running on port **3001** (all files serve HTTP 200).

## What was built

Full vanilla-JS space shooter in `/workspace/space-shooter/` — **11 files**, 2286 lines across 8 JS modules, matching the exact structure you specified. No libraries, no frameworks — plain `<script>` tags loaded in dependency order (config > audio > particles > background > enemies > player > ui > game), global objects so `game.js` (the single entry point) can call `Game.init()` on load.

**Verified via headless runtime tests** — all JS files pass syntax check, all modules load cleanly in order, and a simulated browser sandbox drove the real game loop for **3000 frames with zero runtime errors**. Confirmed working: module loading, `Game.init()` bootstrap, full gameplay (55+ enemies spawned, collisions firing, kills, score/combo accumulation, 5 kills → level 1→2), boss wave at level % 5 (mini-swarm of small octopi + boss spawn), player death → gameover, restart loop.

**Key implementation points from your spec, implemented:**
- Canvas setup in `game.js` `init()`: `canvas.width=innerWidth`, `height=innerHeight`, `ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled=false`, resize listener ✓
- Enemy sizes: small=36, medium=48, baby=20, boss=150 ✓
- Bullet speeds: tier1=8, tier2=10, tier3=12, tier4=14 ✓
- Mouse lerp factor **0.35** ✓
- Circle-to-circle collision (`dx²+dy² < (r1+r2)²`), bullet radius=bullet width, enemy radius=size/2, player+30px buffer ✓
- All octopus types rendered from **2D pixel grids via `fillRect`** (no `ctx.arc()` for the enemy), cell size derived from enemy size ✓
- 4-layer parallax background all scrolling **downward** (stars/nebula/planets/comets) with mouse-reactive depth ✓
- `Particles.draw(ctx)` called in the main draw loop; engine trails in `player.update()`, bullet trails in `updateBullets()`, spark/ink/explosion effects ✓
- Hit feedback: 3-frame white flash, spark particles, floating damage numbers rising 60px over 1s, hit sound ✓
- HUD: 20px monospace, score (x=20,y=40), level (center,y=40), combo (right edge,y=40), health bar bottom ✓
- Web Audio API procedural sounds for all the required events ✓
- Start/gameover/pause (ESC) screens with monospace UI ✓
- README with description, `python3 -m http.server 3001` instructions, controls, and structure ✓

## How to run

The server is already live:

```bash
cd /workspace/space-shooter
python3 -m http.server 3001
```

Then open **http://localhost:3001**. Click to start, hold left-click to fire, move the mouse to steer, ESC to pause. Click "CLICK TO RESTART" on the gameover screen to restart.

Note: `index.html`'s CSS is loaded via `css/styles.css` which I created (full-screen canvas, hidden cursor during gameplay, no-select, overflow hidden).

**Things I had to fix during the build:** (1) the game loop only queued `requestAnimationFrame` once — fixed to re-queue each frame, (2) a `rgba(...)` color regex in the nebula rendering didn't match the stored color format, and (3) an enemy color-key lookup assumed `enemyMedium` while config defines `enemyMed` — I added an explicit color map. All verified working in the 3000-frame test run.

spec.evidence: an array literal holding speeds 8, 10, 12, 14 in order
dx*dx + dy*dy (member operands, x**2 and Math.pow(x, 2) too) or Math.hypot in source
9 0/1 grid rows or grids (>=8 cells) found
string literal containing #0D1117, or #0D1117 in any .css/.html
'monospace' in a JS/TS string or any .css/.html (V3: the JetBrains Mono TTF in public/fonts)
imports three-flatland; Sprite2D and SpriteGroup used

evidence.threshold: std >= 4 and >= 0.5% pixels off the mode color

evidence.rule: title and CLICK TO START in DOM text or fillText, whitespace ignored

pointer alternates x=30%/70% three times (300 ms of game time each); per side the median of its 3 shots; object = pixels within +-40 px of the pointer, bottom 45%, differing by > 90 between the two medians; passes when >= 100 of them are found again (same colour < 60, or an object pixel there) at the pointer's displacement (+-48 px, +-24 px vertical) in BOTH windows

evidence.threshold: paused < 0.3 and resumed >= 0.3 (or the game ended after the resume), or PAUSE text; not measured if GAME OVER showed before ESC

evidence.rule: DOM boxes: SCORE left 20, LEVEL centered, COMBO right, y=40 inside the box, 20px monospace; COMBO judged only when a visible COMBO element exists (v3)

determinism.paced: game time advanced in 50 ms steps, paced to the wall clock

changes.change: the browser run is DETERMINISTIC: the page's Math.random is seeded (browser_check.RNG_SEED) and its clock is Playwright's fake clock, paused and advanced by the script in 50 ms steps paced to the wall clock, so the game gets exactly 60 frames per game second whatever the host's load; screenshots are taken at fixed GAME times. v2 waited in wall-clock seconds while the game's own Math.random chose the enemies
changes.spec: ship follows mouse cursor smoothly / pause with ESC key / HUD: score (top left), level (top center), combo counter (top right) -- all at y=40
changes.why: v2 on the UNCHANGED reference fixture, 5 grades: mousemove_moves_ship 1/5, hud_positions 1/5, esc_pause 0/5 (3/3 on 2026-09-24); v0f@p2's mousemove flipped between two grades (SELF-IMPROVEMENT-LOG #60)

changes.change: after clicking a start ELEMENT the grader undoes its own scrollIntoView (window.scrollTo(0, 0)) and nudges the pointer 1 px and back, as a player's hand does; v2 left the page scrolled and the pointer still
changes.spec: start screen: ... "CLICK TO START" text / ship follows mouse cursor
changes.why: the reference's Start button is below the fold at 1280x720; the grader's scroll (32 px) shifted every later screenshot and left the pointer below the canvas, so the ship flew to (0, 0) until the mouse next moved

changes.change: the pointer alternates left / right THREE times (x 30% / 70%, 300 ms of game time each); per side the pixel-wise median of its 3 shots; the object at the pointer (pixels within +-40 px of it, bottom 45%, that differ between pointer-here and pointer-away) must be found again -- same colours, or the same object shape -- where the pointer went (>= 100 px, both directions); NOT MEASURED (None) when the game was over during the sequence. v2: one left/right pair, bright-pixel or cyan centroid shift > 25% of the width. Calibrated on 2 games and the same 2 with the ship's lerp zeroed (grade.ship_follows docstring; n = 1 each)
changes.spec: ship follows mouse cursor smoothly; ship.x += (mouseX - ship.x) * 0.35 per frame
changes.why: v2's centroids were moved by a cyan planet and by descending enemies (v0f@p2, index/octopus/grades_backup_20260926-221204/v0f-V0-xhigh-1_p2: the ship visibly moved 243 -> 1036 px, check failed), and failed whenever the ship had died (reference). 30% / 70% (v2: 19% / 81%) lie between the 20/40/60/80% columns of a four-enemy W/(n+1) wave; parked at 19% the reference's ship died under its column-1 ink blobs in the first v3 trial

changes.change: ESC is pressed 2.3 s of game time after the start; NOT MEASURED (None) when GAME OVER was showing before ESC; if the game ends after the second ESC, the resume half counts as met (the game ran). Thresholds unchanged
changes.spec: pause with ESC key
changes.why: v2 pressed ESC on the reference's GAME OVER screen (its ship had died) and failed it 5/5

changes.change: the start screen's canvas text must be absent from what was drawn SINCE the click (browser_check fill_since, from 100 ms after it); v2 read the texts drawn in the last 1500 ms, which v3's 500 ms of game time after the click would still contain
changes.spec: start screen: ... "CLICK TO START" text
changes.why: found by the v3 stability run: v0f@p2's state failed 5/5 with its HUD drawn and the start text last drawn at the click

changes.change: JUDGEMENT CALL (operator to confirm): COMBO's position is judged when a COMBO text was drawn at all; a game that shows the counter only while a combo is running passes on SCORE and LEVEL (the evidence says combo_drawn: false; combo_counter still checks the counter exists). V1/V2 read the DOM HUD right after the 30 s of play, not after the game-over attempt
changes.spec: HUD: score (top left), level (top center), combo counter (top right) -- all at y=40 with 20px font; combo multiplier for consecutive kills without getting hit
changes.why: the reference draws COMBO only when combo > 1; v2 passed it only on the 1 of 5 grades whose random play happened to chain two kills

changes.change: a check listed in grade.FLAKY (not 5/5 or 0/5 on an unchanged state in bench/octopus/stability.py) keeps its result in the row, marked `flaky`, and is left out of the headline (spec_passed / spec_failed / spec_total); spec_flaky lists it
changes.spec: (measurement hygiene, not a spec item)
changes.why: a measurement that flips on unchanged code is not a measurement

- **4 octopus types** + boss with multi-phase health bar
- **UNLEASH MODE**: big/boss kill → orb → 5s white-hot mode, 3x score, spread beams, ring countdown, chromatic aberration

final_event.text:
The game is complete and the server is running on port **3001** (all files serve HTTP 200).

## What was built

Full vanilla-JS space shooter in `/workspace/space-shooter/` — **11 files**, 2286 lines across 8 JS modules, matching the exact structure you specified. No libraries, no frameworks — plain `<script>` tags loaded in dependency order (config > audio > particles > background > enemies > player > ui > game), global objects so `game.js` (the single entry point) can call `Game.init()` on load.

**Verified via headless runtime tests** — all JS files pass syntax check, all modules load cleanly in order, and a simulated browser sandbox drove the real game loop for **3000 frames with zero runtime errors**. Confirmed working: module loading, `Game.init()` bootstrap, full gameplay (55+ enemies spawned, collisions firing, kills, score/combo accumulation, 5 kills → level 1→2), boss wave at level % 5 (mini-swarm of small octopi + boss spawn), player death → gameover, restart loop.

**Key implementation points from your spec, implemented:**
- Canvas setup in `game.js` `init()`: `canvas.width=innerWidth`, `height=innerHeight`, `ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled=false`, resize listener ✓
- Enemy sizes: small=36, medium=48, baby=20, boss=150 ✓
- Bullet speeds: tier1=8, tier2=10, tier3=12, tier4=14 ✓
- Mouse lerp factor **0.35** ✓
- Circle-to-circle collision (`dx²+dy² < (r1+r2)²`), bullet radius=bullet width, enemy radius=size/2, player+30px buffer ✓
- All octopus types rendered from **2D pixel grids via `fillRect`** (no `ctx.arc()` for the enemy), cell size derived from enemy size ✓
- 4-layer parallax background all scrolling **downward** (stars/nebula/planets/comets) with mouse-reactive depth ✓
- `Particles.draw(ctx)` called in the main draw loop; engine trails in `player.update()`, bullet trails in `updateBullets()`, spark/ink/explosion effects ✓
- Hit feedback: 3-frame white flash, spark particles, floating damage numbers rising 60px over 1s, hit sound ✓
- HUD: 20px monospace, score (x=20,y=40), level (center,y=40), combo (right edge,y=40), health bar bottom ✓
- Web Audio API procedural sounds for all the required events ✓
- Start/gameover/pause (ESC) screens with monospace UI ✓
- README with description, `python3 -m http.server 3001` instructions, controls, and structure ✓

## How to run

The server is already live:

```bash
cd /workspace/space-shooter
python3 -m http.server 3001
```

Then open **http://localhost:3001**. Click to start, hold left-click to fire, move the mouse to steer, ESC to pause. Click "CLICK TO RESTART" on the gameover screen to restart.

Note: `index.html`'s CSS is loaded via `css/styles.css` which I created (full-screen canvas, hidden cursor during gameplay, no-select, overflow hidden).

**Things I had to fix during the build:** (1) the game loop only queued `requestAnimationFrame` once — fixed to re-queue each frame, (2) a `rgba(...)` color regex in the nebula rendering didn't match the stored color format, and (3) an enemy color-key lookup assumed `enemyMedium` while config defines `enemyMed` — I added an explicit color map. All verified working in the 3000-frame test run.
